Maria P.: Hey team — quick question. Im moving to Spain for 4 months for a project (still on US payroll). Do I stay on the Redwood US health plan during that time? Any steps I need to take for coverage abroad? :airplane:

Alex (Eng): I did short-term remote in EU last year — US plans usually cover emergency care but not routine local providers. You might need travel or local insurance for regular visits. cc @Jen - People Ops

Jen - People Ops: Hi Maria — short answer: you can remain on the US plan as long as youre still an active Redwood employee, but there are a few important caveats about provider networks and claims when abroad. Posting a quick checklist below.

Benefits Bot: Automated reminder: international travel under 6 months typically remains on US benefits; file address change in Workday if outside the US >30 days.

Jen - People Ops: Checklist: 1) Keep your Redwood digital ID card (we can email a PDF). 2) For emergency care abroad, the US plan usually covers medically necessary emergency services — keep receipts and get itemized bills. 3) For non-emergency care, youll likely be out-of-network — consider short-term international medical insurance for routine care. 4) If a foreign provider files a claim locally, we may need the itemized bill + translation + proof of payment to submit to the insurer. 5) Telehealth: use Redwoods telemedicine vendor for non-urgent consults to avoid out-of-network bills.

Maria P.: Got it — do you have an example of what the insurer needs for a foreign claim? Also, can you send the digital ID card?

Jen - People Ops: Example claim package (attach these when you submit to benefits@redwood.com):
```
- Scanned itemized invoice from provider (date of service, diagnosis, CPT/SSS if available)
- Proof of payment (card receipt, bank statement)
- Translation if not in English (simple attestation ok)
- Patient name + DOB + Redwood employee ID
```
Ill email you the digital ID card now.

Alex (Eng): Also keep photocopies of passports for cross-border billing weirdness. Had to submit a passport page once for a claim.

Maria P.: Thanks — one more: is there any change to premium deductions or benefits eligibility if Im abroad?

Jen - People Ops: No change to premiums or eligibility while youre on payroll. If your stay extends beyond 6 months we need to run a benefits impact review (visa/status dependent). If you plan to enroll a local dependent or go on a local plan, we can coordinate.

Benefits Bot: Action items for Maria P.: 1) Confirm dates and update temporary address in Workday. 2) Email benefits@redwood.com for your digital ID card PDF. 3) If you expect routine care, consider short-term international coverage and send quotes to benefits for pre-approval.

Maria P.: Thanks @Jen - People Ops and team. Ill update Workday and send an email with dates. Appreciate the clear steps! :pray:
